## Question 1

### (a)

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(nlme)
library(knitr)
load("WtLoss.Rdata")
wtloss$diet <- factor(wtloss$diet)
```

```{r fit}
# (i) random intercepts only
m1 <- lme(weight ~ diet * time, random = ~ 1 | id, data = wtloss)
# (ii) random intercepts and random slopes
m2 <- lme(weight ~ diet * time, random = ~ 1 + time | id, data = wtloss)
```

```{r table, echo=FALSE}
f <- function(e, l, u, d = 2) sprintf(paste0("%.", d, "f (%.", d, "f, %.", d, "f)"), e, l, u)
fp <- function(p) ifelse(p < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p))

col <- function(m) {
  fe <- intervals(m)$fixed
  d  <- ifelse(grepl("time", rownames(fe)), 3, 2)
  re <- intervals(m)$reStruct$id
  s  <- intervals(m)$sigma
  est <- c(mapply(f, fe[, 2], fe[, 1], fe[, 3], d),
           f(re[1, 2], re[1, 1], re[1, 3]),
           if (nrow(re) > 1) c(f(re[2, 2], re[2, 1], re[2, 3], 3),
                               f(re[3, 2], re[3, 1], re[3, 3])) else c("—", "—"),
           f(s[2], s[1], s[3]))
  p <- c(fp(summary(m)$tTable[, "p-value"]), rep("", 4))
  cbind(est, p)
}

tab <- data.frame(
  c("Intercept", "Diet 1 (vs. diet 0)", "Diet 2 (vs. diet 0)", "Time (months)",
    "Diet 1 × time", "Diet 2 × time",
    "SD of random intercepts", "SD of random slopes",
    "Corr(random intercept, slope)", "Residual SD"),
  col(m1), col(m2), row.names = NULL)
names(tab) <- c("", "Model (i): Estimate (95% CI)", "p-value",
                "Model (ii): Estimate (95% CI)", "p-value")
kable(tab, align = "lcccc",
      caption = paste("Linear mixed models for weight (lbs) in 120 patients.",
                      "Model (i): random intercepts; model (ii): random intercepts and slopes.",
                      "Diet 0 (counseling at baseline only) is the reference group."))
```

### Interpretation of model (ii)

**Fixed effects**

* **Intercept (250.99):** the mean weight at baseline for patients in diet 0 is 250.99 lbs.
* **Diet 1 (−0.70):** at baseline, mean weight in diet 1 is 0.70 lbs lower than in diet 0 (not significant, p = 0.34).
* **Diet 2 (−2.69):** at baseline, mean weight in diet 2 is 2.69 lbs lower than in diet 0 (p < 0.001).
* **Time (0.019):** in diet 0, mean weight changes by 0.019 lbs per month (not significant, p = 0.61), so there is no evidence of weight change in diet 0.
* **Diet 1 × time (−0.102):** the rate of change in mean weight is 0.102 lbs/month lower in diet 1 than in diet 0 (p = 0.044), i.e., diet 1 loses weight faster.
* **Diet 2 × time (−0.491):** the rate of change in mean weight is 0.491 lbs/month lower in diet 2 than in diet 0 (p < 0.001), i.e., diet 2 loses weight fastest.

**Variance components**

* **SD of random intercepts (3.20):** within the same diet group, patients' baseline weights vary around the group mean with SD 3.20 lbs.
* **SD of random slopes (0.162):** within the same diet group, patients' rates of weight change vary around the group mean slope with SD 0.162 lbs/month.
* **Correlation (−0.40):** patients with higher baseline weight tend to have more negative slopes (lose weight faster).
* **Residual SD (1.00):** a patient's observed weight at a visit varies around their own fitted line with SD 1.00 lbs.

### (b)

Let $\mathbf{b}_i = (b_{0i}, b_{1i})^T \sim N(\mathbf{0}, \mathbf{G})$ with $\mathbf{G} = \begin{pmatrix} \sigma^2_{b0} & \sigma_{b01} \\ \sigma_{b01} & \sigma^2_{b1} \end{pmatrix}$.

* $H_0$: $\sigma^2_{b1} = 0$ (and therefore $\sigma_{b01} = 0$), i.e., the random intercept model (i) is adequate.
* $H_1$: $\sigma^2_{b1} > 0$, i.e., the random intercept and slope model (ii) is needed.

```{r sim, fig.height=4.5, fig.width=7}
sim <- simulate(m1, m2 = list(random = ~ 1 + time | id),
                nsim = 1000, seed = 1504, method = "REML")
lrt_null <- pmax(2 * (sim$alt$REML[, "logLik"] - sim$null$REML[, "logLik"]), 0)
lrt_obs  <- as.numeric(2 * (logLik(m2) - logLik(m1)))

q_sim <- quantile(lrt_null, 0.95)
q1 <- qchisq(0.95, 1); q2 <- qchisq(0.95, 2)

hist(lrt_null, breaks = 40, freq = FALSE, xlim = c(0, 12), ylim = c(0, 1),
     col = "grey85", border = "white", xlab = "LRT statistic",
     main = "Simulated null distribution of the LRT statistic")
curve(dchisq(x, 1), add = TRUE, col = "blue", lwd = 2, from = 0.01)
curve(dchisq(x, 2), add = TRUE, col = "red",  lwd = 2)
abline(v = q_sim, lty = 2, lwd = 2)
abline(v = q1, lty = 2, lwd = 2, col = "blue")
abline(v = q2, lty = 2, lwd = 2, col = "red")
legend("topright", bty = "n", lty = c(1, 1, 2, 2, 2), lwd = 2,
       col = c("blue", "red", "black", "blue", "red"),
       legend = c("Chi-square(1)", "Chi-square(2)",
                  sprintf("Simulated 95th pct = %.2f", q_sim),
                  sprintf("Chi-square(1) 95th pct = %.2f", q1),
                  sprintf("Chi-square(2) 95th pct = %.2f", q2)))

c(observed_LRT = lrt_obs, simulated_p_value = mean(lrt_null >= lrt_obs))
```

The observed LRT statistic is `r round(lrt_obs, 1)`, far above the simulated 95th percentile (`r round(q_sim, 2)`), and none of the 1000 simulated null statistics are this large (p < 0.001). We reject $H_0$: the random intercept model is not adequate, and the random intercept and slope model fits the data significantly better.
